justice: The street allocates substantial space to motor vehicles with multiple wide asphalt lanes, while pedestrian space is limited to side sidewalks, indicating an uneven distribution of street space across user types.

Streetlights are installed along the corridor, supporting nighttime visibility and general traffic safety.

Parked cars line both curbs, and vehicles are also stopped near the right edge of the carriageway, which can create dooring or visibility conflicts for pedestrians and any cyclists sharing the edge space.

sustainability: Rows of street trees and landscaped strips along both sides provide some green infrastructure and modest ecological benefit.
No dedicated bike lane, bus lane, or visible bus stop is present in the image, so support for low-carbon travel modes appears limited in this specific view.

There are no visible permeable paving areas, bioswales, or rainwater management features that would indicate stronger stormwater-sensitive design.
aesthetics: The corridor has a clean and orderly appearance, with smooth asphalt, aligned streetlights, and consistent roadside planting.

comfort: Tree planting exists along both sidewalks, but shade coverage over the walking paths appears limited, so thermal comfort is only moderate in sunny conditions.
